_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel just shattered the all-time record — $5.967/gal for the week of 9/7, up a brutal 36.8 cents — so hold firm on the full fuel surcharge, you've earned it. Spot's showing broad strength again too: national all-in sits near $3.44/mi (+47% YoY, first equipment-wide gain since May) and reefer's leading the charge at $3.54/mi as Yakima cherry season tightens Northeast lanes ($9.9k-$10.8k a load) — keep pushing produce hard and don't discount dry van just because it's lagging on an all-in basis.

_sourcing.status: TWELFTH straight cycle with the WebFetch/curl egress block confirmed session-wide (unchanged) — see refreshBlockers. This is the strongest refresh in weeks: diesel hit a NEW ALL-TIME RECORD, $5.967/gal for the week ending 2026-09-07, up $0.368 w/w (arithmetic checks: 5.599+0.368=5.967), breaking the prior June-2022 record of $5.810 by ~15.7c, per EIA data corroborated across Logistics Management ('National diesel average hits an all-time high, for the week of September 7, reports EIA') and weeklydiesel.com's DOE tracker (independently returned the same $5.967 figure and the same 'series record high' framing). asOf advanced to 2026-09-07 on this clean multi-source confirmation. Also finally refreshed the 5-week-stale spotAllIn field: FreightWaves' SONAR National Truckload Index (NTI) — the actual national blended all-in benchmark — read $3.44/mi in a Sept 9 FreightWaves article ('Truckload Volumes Drop 15% — But Spot Rates Stay Hot'), up ~0.5% on the day and +47% YoY vs $2.29/mi a year ago; this exact figure (with the same 47% YoY and half-percent daily-move detail) reproduced identically across two independent targeted searches, which is the strongest corroboration bar this desk has hit on this field to date. Reefer modality/commodity rates promoted to $3.54/mi (TheTrucker, citing DAT: 'Reefer spot rates climb 9 cents to $3.54 a mile ahead of Labor Day,' wk ending 9/5, explicitly all-in/boosted-by-fuel) — reproduced across three separate searches with consistent wording. Yakima→Northeast lane promoted off a genuinely new source type: USDA AMS's National Truck Rate Report (fvwtrk.pdf / agtransport.usda.gov), summarized by IndexBox for the week ended 2026-09-08, giving Baltimore $9,900 and Boston $10,800 per-load midpoints from Yakima Valley/Wenatchee — reproduced identically (same two dollar figures) across two independent searches, a materially cleaner signal than the percentage-only DAT blog commentary that blocked promotion the last six cycles. Trend moved from 'flat' to 'up': diesel spiked to a record, reefer climbed, dry van and flatbed linehaul both ticked up, and FleetOwner reported the broker-posted rate 'jumped just over 9 cents last week... for the first time since May' across all three equipment types — a genuinely uniform up signal this time, not the mixed picture from last cycle. Dry van modality/spotAllIn-equivalent all-in figure and the Atlanta→Miami lane were NOT promoted this cycle — see per-field notes.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE. $5.967/gal for the week ending 2026-09-07, up $0.368 w/w — a new EIA series record high, surpassing the June 2022 record ($5.810) by ~15.7c. Confirmed across Logistics Management (explicitly EIA-sourced, headline 'hits an all-time high') and weeklydiesel.com's DOE weekly tracker, both independently returning the same $5.967 figure. Checked for a fresher week-ending-9/14 reading: EIA's next release is 9/15 (today) and hadn't surfaced in search results as of this refresh, so 9/7 is the freshest published EIA number. Note: GasBuddy's daily retail survey separately claimed $6.183 for 9/14 and a dailyfuels.com aggregator showed $5.981 — both disregarded as different (non-EIA, non-weekly-on-highway) methodologies inconsistent with this file's series; not used.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: PROMOTED — refreshed after 5 weeks stale. $3.44/mi, per FreightWaves SONAR National Truckload Index (NTI), the national all-in (fuel-inclusive) blended truckload benchmark, dated Sept 9, 2026 ('Truckload Volumes Drop 15% — But Spot Rates Stay Hot'), up ~0.5% on the day and +47% YoY vs $2.29/mi a year ago. This is a refresh of an already-live field (not a new field promotion), and the same specific figure (with matching 47% YoY / half-percent-daily context) reproduced identically across two independent searches — high confidence. Context: NTI's daily sub-index (NTID) spiked to $3.57 on 9/6 before pulling back ~8% to $3.40 on 9/8, and a Sept 11 SONAR market update said rates are 'holding firm even as tender volumes and rejection rates pull back' — consistent with $3.44 as a fair current read, not a one-day spike.
_sourcing.modality: Reefer PROMOTED to $3.54/mi (was $3.33-3.38) — TheTrucker, citing DAT: 'Reefer spot rates climb 9 cents to $3.54 a mile ahead of Labor Day,' week ending 2026-09-05, explicitly described as boosted by higher diesel (i.e., an all-in figure), reproduced consistently across three separate searches. Given as a single point (not a range) since that's the precise sourced figure this cycle; yoy left at +34-38% (a separately-cited '34% YoY reefer' figure from another search sits at the low end, but wasn't cleanly reconcilable to a fresh single number, so not force-updated). Dry van: STILL NOT promoted — every reading found this cycle (DAT dry van linehaul $2.19/mi wk of 9/1, $2.21/mi wk of 9/8, both explicitly 'minus fuel'; a CCJ all-in figure of $2.96/mi surfaced but for the week of 7/26-8/1, which is older than data already on file, not fresher) is either linehaul-only or stale — no clean current all-in dry van reading exists yet. Carrying $2.47-2.80 forward, flag unchanged. Flatbed and LTL/Intermodal: no new all-in data this cycle, unchanged (flatbed linehaul was reported up to $2.66/mi loaded for wk of 9/4, +31.2% YoY, but that's linehaul-only, not convertible to all-in without fabricating the surcharge).
_sourcing.commodityRates: Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce PROMOTED to 3.54 (from 3.35), tracking the reefer modality promotion above — both commodities are reefer-moved and the file's convention ties them to the reefer rpm. General Dry Freight (2.47), Coiled Steel (3.57), and High-Value Electronics (2.60) carry forward unchanged — no underlying dry van or flatbed reprice this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA → Northeast (reefer) PROMOTED to $9.9k-$10.8k/load (from $8.7k-$10.6k), ending a SIX-cycle carry-forward streak. Source: USDA AMS's National Truck Rate Report (the fvwtrk.pdf specialty-crops truck rate series published via agtransport.usda.gov), summarized by IndexBox for the week ended 2026-09-08, giving per-load midpoints of $9,900 to Baltimore and $10,800 to Boston from the Yakima Valley/Wenatchee District — both figures reproduced identically across two independent searches, a materially different and more traceable source type (USDA primary data, not a DAT blog percentage) than what's blocked this lane the last six cycles. Range built from the two named Northeast cities actually cited (Baltimore/Boston); did not include the separately-cited Atlanta ($9,200) or Chicago ($7,100) midpoints since those aren't 'Northeast.' Atlanta, GA → Miami, FL: NOT promoted — only generic evergreen lane-guide pages ('$2.95/mile FTL, verified July 2026') and percentage-only DAT blog commentary ('Miami up 12% in late August') surfaced, neither meeting the clean-dated-absolute bar; carried forward unchanged. Memphis, TN → Atlanta, GA: no new data searched/found this cycle, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten to lead with diesel's new all-time record (coaching: hold firm on the full surcharge) and the spotAllIn refresh finally landing (national all-in near $3.44/mi, +47% YoY, broad first-since-May gain), with reefer's $3.54/mi and the newly-promoted Yakima Northeast lane figures reinforcing the push-produce-hard coaching; kept a soft caution on dry van since its all-in figure is still unrefreshed.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Dry van's modality range is still the open item — every reading found remains linehaul-only or stale; needs a clean, independently-dated, all-in reading before promoting past $2.47-2.80. Atlanta→Miami lane still needs a clean dated absolute $/mi from trade press or DAT Trendlines proper, not a lane-guide page or a percentage delta. Reefer's yoy range (+34-38%) is carried at the same figure as last cycle — worth a dedicated yoy-specific search next cycle now that the rpm itself has moved.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed. WebFetch to www.eia.gov returned 'EGRESS_BLOCKED' immediately. Raw curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/, https://www.dat.com/, and the https://en.wikipedia.org/ control all returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (exit code 56), with the agent-proxy logging all three as connect_rejected/organization policy. Confirms the block is unchanged across all TWELVE weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 09-15. WebSearch remains the only working channel, but this cycle it delivered the cleanest, most-corroborated batch yet: diesel's new record ($5.967, two independent EIA-citing sources), the first spotAllIn refresh in 5 weeks (FreightWaves SONAR NTI $3.44, reproduced identically across two searches), a reefer promotion ($3.54, reproduced across three searches), and the first lane promotion in six cycles (Yakima→Northeast off a genuine USDA AMS primary source, reproduced across two searches). Still could not cleanly promote dry van's all-in modality range or the Atlanta→Miami lane — see per-field notes. Broader web-fetch access to eia.gov, dat.com/trendlines, agtransport.usda.gov, or trade outlets directly (rather than relying on WebSearch's synthesized summaries) would let those two remaining fields get the same primary-source treatment the rest of the file now has, and would let this desk pull the actual USDA fvwtrk.pdf directly instead of via a third-party IndexBox summary.
